LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command sources the PKGBUILD file and executes only code in the global/top-level scope. In this PKGBUILD, the top-level scope consists exclusively of standard variable definitions: `pkgbase`, `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `makedepends`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. There are no command substitutions, network requests, file operations, or other executable code at the top level.

All other code in this file consists of function definitions (`_build()`, `build()`, `_package()`, and `package_*` functions) which are not executed during sourcing—they would only run when their names are explicitly called later in the packaging process. These function definitions contain operations like `luarocks`, `mkdir`, `sed`, `mv`, and `install`, but they cannot execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

The source URL points to the GitHub repository for the openresty/lua-cjson project, which is the legitimate upstream source. There is no obfuscation, suspicious downloads, or malicious code in the global scope that would execute during this specific command.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Only standard variable definitions in global scope</summary>
</security_assessment>
